title: Model Tells You Where to Merge: Adaptive KV Cache Merging for LLMs on Long-Context Tasks

contributions.purpose: Compress the KV cache of LLMs for long-context inference under constrained memory budgets without significant performance degradation.
contributions.mechanism: KVMerger: formulates KV cache merging as a constrained clustering problem solved by a specialized greedy merging-set identification algorithm, then applies a Gaussian kernel weighted merging function to merge key/value states within each set (as opposed to eviction/quantization).
contributions.evaluation: On Llama2-7B/13B-chat and Mistral-7B-instruct, with 50% and 35% KV cache budgets, KVMerger achieves superior performance vs H2O and CaM on LongBench, ZeroScrolls, and Needle-in-a-Haystack; reports comparable performance or much smaller gap vs full cache.
contributions.domain: Efficient LLM inference / KV cache compression
contributions.source_quote: we develop an effective merging set identification algorithm to identify suitable KV states for merging and a Gaussian kernel weighted merging algorithm to selectively merge all states within each merging set.

contributions.purpose: Provide the empirical observation that motivates and justifies the merging design.
contributions.mechanism: Analysis of cosine similarity of key states across attention heads and layers; investigate the root cause of the similarity phenomenon.
contributions.evaluation: Finding: key states exhibit high cosine similarity at the token level within a single sequence; and KV cache sparsity (from a similarity perspective) is independent of the dataset and persistent at the model level.
contributions.domain: Efficient LLM inference / KV cache compression
contributions.source_quote: We introduce an intriguing observation that key states share a high similarity at the token level within a single sequence, as an important complementary to the previous observations concerning high query states similarity (Dai et al., 2024) and intra-layer KV cache similarity (Liu et al., 2024).

self_declared_provenance.quote: an important complementary to the previous observations concerning high query states similarity (Dai et al., 2024) and intra-layer KV cache similarity (Liu et al., 2024).
Different from quantization, this work studies compression of KV cache via states merging, which is complementary to quantization.
Very recently, KV cache merging has emerged a complementary method of eviction (Zhang et al.). Unlike eviction-based methods, KV cache merging technique does not strictly remove key and value states.

notes: Authors self-describe results as 'comparable performance or much smaller performance gap compared to full cache budgets' (not strictly a win over full cache). ICLR 2025 reject. Positioned as one of the pioneering works on KV cache merging.
